raw_case_text:
A 38-year-old HIV-positive male, who was not on antiretroviral treatment, presented with a right-sided conjunctival mass for an uncertain period of time. On examination, he was in good health and did not have any soft-tissue masses elsewhere. Ophthalmic examination revealed right eye hyperaemia together with a raised conjunctival lesion noted on the medial aspect, extending on to the cornea. He was found to have normal vision. The clinical assessment was that of an invasive squamous cell carcinoma.
The patient underwent a monoblock excision of the mass with cryotherapy applied to the base. Clinically, the margins were thought to be free of tumour. The tissue was submitted for histopathological evaluation. The patient had not returned for his follow-up appointment.
The excised specimen submitted for histopathological examination consisted of a single, unorientated fragment of tissue measuring 7 mm x 4 mm x 3 mm. The specimen was processed in its entirety.
Microscopic examination revealed a single portion of tissue surfaced by intact squamous mucosa. At one edge of the surface mucosa, mild dysplasia was noted. Within the underlying tissue, however, a spindle cell proliferation was present. This proliferation consisted of fascicles of spindle cells displaying varying degrees of atypia. The cells were large and hyperchromatic. Focally, tumour cells contained perinuclear vacuoles. Mitotic activity was apparent with up to 14 mitotic figures noted in 10 high-powered fields (Figure 1). Definitive lymphovascular and perineural infiltration was not documented in the submitted specimen. The tumour measured 2 mm in thickness and was clear of the peripheral surgical resection margins.
Immunohistochemistry for cytokeratins (AE1/3, MNF116, 34BE12, CK5/6) and a p63 stain were negative, thus excluding the most likely diagnosis of a spindle cell carcinoma. Melanocytic markers (S100, MiTF, Melan-A and HMB-45) were negative and excluded a diagnosis of a malignant melanoma. Kaposi sarcoma was excluded with negative staining for Human Herpes Virus-8 (HHV8) and CD31. A desmin stain was positive in the neoplastic cells. Smooth muscle actin (SMA), muscle-specific actin (MSA) and h-Caldesmon stains were positive in tumour cells (Figure 2). Myogenin and Myo-D1 stains were both negative, thus excluding a rhabdomyosarcoma. Epstein-Barr encoding region (EBER) in-situ hybridisation was negative. A final diagnosis of a conjunctival leiomyosarcoma was rendered.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 38-year-old male presenting with a painless, raised mass on the right conjunctiva of uncertain duration.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a slowly enlarging, painless mass involving the medial aspect of the right eye for an uncertain duration. He reported no visual disturbance, ocular trauma, foreign body sensation, or prior ophthalmologic interventions.
subjective.past_medical_history: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection, untreated (not currently receiving antiretroviral therapy); otherwise in good health with no known chronic medical conditions.
subjective.review_of_systems: Right ocular hyperemia and visible growth; denies eye pain, diplopia, reduced visual acuity, systemic soft-tissue masses, constitutional symptoms, or weight loss.

objective.physical_examination: General physical examination: Good general health, no peripheral lymphadenopathy or cutaneous soft-tissue lesions. Ophthalmologic examination: Visual acuity normal bilaterally; right eye demonstrated conjunctival hyperemia with a raised, fleshy conjunctival lesion on the medial aspect extending across the limbus onto the cornea.
objective.advanced_workup: Surgical pathology of excised conjunctival lesion (7 mm x 4 mm x 3 mm, tumor thickness 2 mm): Histopathology demonstrated intact overlying squamous mucosa with focal mild dysplasia, overlying a fascicular spindle cell proliferation exhibiting nuclear pleomorphism, hyperchromasia, focal perinuclear vacuolization, and high mitotic activity (up to 14 mitoses per 10 high-power fields), with clear surgical margins and absence of lymphovascular or perineural invasion. Immunohistochemistry: Positive for desmin, smooth muscle actin (SMA), muscle-specific actin (MSA), and h-caldesmon; negative for cytokeratins (AE1/3, MNF116, 34betaE12, CK5/6), p63, melanocytic markers (S100, MiTF, Melan-A, HMB-45), vascular/Kaposi markers (HHV-8, CD31), skeletal muscle markers (myogenin, Myo-D1), and Epstein-Barr virus-encoded RNA (EBER in-situ hybridization).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Primary conjunctival leiomyosarcoma (smooth muscle malignancy) in an untreated HIV-positive male; squamous cell carcinoma, malignant melanoma, Kaposi sarcoma, and rhabdomyosarcoma were ruled out by immunohistochemistry.
Plan & Outcome: Managed with complete wide local monoblock surgical excision of the conjunctival mass with adjuvant cryotherapy applied to the surgical bed, achieving microscopically negative resection margins. The patient was scheduled for routine oncologic and ophthalmologic surveillance, but was subsequently lost to follow-up.
